title: Affine locus of a quasi-compact flat monomorphism contains its image
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact flat monomorphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], where monomorphism means that postcomposition is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)$ for every scheme $T$. There is an open subscheme $U\subseteq S$ [def-weil-open-immersion] containing $f(|X|)$ such that the induced morphism $X\to U$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. No quasi-affineness of $X$, quasi-separatedness of $S$, local finite presentation of $f$, or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: §1 Proposition 1.5(i), printed p.3; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $E=f(|X|)$. By [lem-sfb-qc-flat-monomorphism-ringed-image], $f$ identifies $X$ with the ringed subspace induced by $S$ on $E$, in particular with the subspace topology on $E$. Fix $x\in X$ and choose an affine open $A\subseteq S$ containing $f(x)$. The open subscheme $f^{-1}(A)$ is a scheme; choose an affine chart $V$ of it containing $x$, using [def-pc-scheme]. Since $V$ is open in the subspace $E\cap A$, there is an open $W\subseteq A$ with $E\cap W=V$. Under the ringed-subspace identification, $f^{-1}(W)=V$ and the restriction $f|_V:V\to W$ is the induced morphism.

source.place: §1, Proposition 1.5(i), printed p.3, first sentence of the proof (reduce to affine target and choose an affine neighbourhood in X); primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof.text: The structure map $A\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). An open-subscheme inclusion is monic directly from [def-weil-open-immersion]: its injective continuous map determines a lift uniquely, and its structure sheaf is a restriction, so the sheaf map of the lift is also determined. Thus $W\times_AW\cong W$, by the fibre-product universal property. Equivalently the diagonal of $W$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is the pullback of the diagonal of $A$ along $W\times W\to A\times A$. It is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Hence $W$ is separated in the sense of [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $V$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism] makes $f|_V:V\to W$ affine. By [pqf-def-affine-morphism], every affine open $B\subseteq W$ has affine inverse image $f^{-1}(B)\subseteq V$.

source.place: §1, Proposition 1.5(i), printed p.3, proof: W is contained in an affine target, hence separated, and the affine-source morphism is affine; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof.text: Let $U$ be the union in $S$ of the opens $W$ obtained in step 1, over all $x\in X$. Then $U$ is open and contains $f(|X|)$, so $f$ factors through the open subscheme $U$ by restricting its continuous map and structure-sheaf homomorphism. For any $y\in U$, choose one such $W$ containing $y$ and then an affine chart $B$ of the open subscheme $W$ containing $y$, using [def-pc-scheme]; step 2 gives that $f^{-1}(B)$ is affine. These opens $B$ form an affine open covering of $U$ with affine inverse images. Apply [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] to the induced morphism $X\to U$. This proves that $X\to U$ is affine. If $X=\varnothing$, the union is $U=\varnothing$ and the empty affine cover satisfies the same criterion.

source.place: §1, Proposition 1.5(i), printed p.3, conclusion that the union of the local affine locus opens contains f(X); primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof_origin.place: Argument following Raynaud §1 Proposition 1.5(i), printed p.3, read online in the Numdam primary scan; project archival copy WANTED. The open-subscheme separatedness check and affine-cover assembly are expanded using Stacks Tags 01SH, 01S7, 01QR, 01SG and 01S8.

The statement, stmt_deps and source are byte-identical to the base copy, where the item was unsplit. The existential statement follows from Raynaud's 'largest open' and has the same hypotheses (quasi-compact, flat, monomorphism). Step 1: the ringed-image node gives X≅S|_E with the subspace topology, so an affine V⊆f^{-1}(A) equals E∩W for an open W⊆A, and f^{-1}(W)=V by injectivity. Step 2: A→Spec Z is affine (01SH) and so separated (01S7(3)). An open immersion is monic, so Δ_W is the base change of Δ_A and is a closed immersion (01QR). So W is separated as in def-weil-proper-morphism, 01SG(4) gives V→W affine, and f^{-1}(B)⊆V is affine for affine B⊆W. Step 3: the B's form an affine cover of U=∪W, and 01S8 applies; the empty case is handled. Tested X empty, the identity of a non-quasi-separated S, and Spec A_p→Spec A; Raynaud's non-quasi-compact counterexample is excluded by the hypothesis. No duplicate: the quasiaffine-neighbourhood node needs quasi-affine X and quasi-separated T, and the affine-envelope node works on affine S only. All cited nodes from other units are Mathlib leaves, so no tool use needs recording; the worker's split_report tool_uses entry is unneeded but harmless.
